'''María Magdalena González Sánchez''' (born May 8, 1974) is a Mexican astrophysicist, nuclear physicist, researcher, and professor best known for her contributions in [[gamma ray]] research and for being the head of the [[High Altitude Water Cherenkov Experiment]] (HAWC). She has published 90 articles about her field of study in indexed journals. In 2015 she received the [[Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz Recognition]] from the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM).

==Biography==
Dr. González obtained a [[Licentiate (degree)#Mexico|licentiate]] in physics at the [[School of Sciences, UNAM|UNAM Faculty of Sciences]] within the area of [[nuclear physics]]. She earned her PhD in physics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in the area of [[high-energy astrophysics]] while working at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]'s Neutron Science and Technology Group.<ref name=Propel>{{Cite web |url=http://www.spacedaily.com/reports/Biggest_Cosmic_Explosions_Also_May_Propel_Fastest_Objects_In_Universe.html |title=Biggest Cosmic Explosions Also May Propel Fastest Objects In Universe |work=Space Daily |location=Los Alamos |date=2003-08-15 |access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref> She had a postdoctoral residency at the {{ill|Institute of Astronomy, UNAM|es|Instituto de Astronomía de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México|lt=UNAM Institute of Astronomy}}, where she is currently a senior researcher.<ref name=UNAM>{{Cite web |url=http://www.astroscu.unam.mx/IA/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=448&Itemid=88&lang=en |title=Dra. Ma. Magdalena González Sánchez |publisher=[[National Autonomous University of Mexico|UNAM]] Institute of Astronomy |language=Spanish |access-date=2019-06-05 |archive-date=December 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191212003845/http://www.astroscu.unam.mx/IA/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=448&Itemid=88&lang=en |url-status=dead }}</ref>

She is the initiator and collaborator on the [[High Altitude Water Cherenkov Experiment|HAWC]] gamma ray observatory, located on the [[Sierra Negra]] volcano in Puebla, Mexico.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/universidades/unam-involucrada-en-hallazgo-astronomico-mundial.html |title=UNAM, involucrada en hallazgo astronómico mundial |trans-title=UNAM, Involved in Global Astronomical Discovery |work=[[El Financiero (Mexico City)|El Financiero]] |language=Spanish |date=2017-12-28 |access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cienciamx.com/index.php/ciencia/universo/6928-urgente-capta-observatorio-hawc-el-mapa-mas-detallado-del-universo |title=Capta observatorio HAWC el mapa más detallado del universo |trans-title=HAWC Observatory Captures More Detailed Map of the Universe |first=Armando |last=Bonilla |work=México Ciencia y Tecnología |location=Mexico City |language=Spanish |date=2015-04-21 |access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref> She was also a collaborator and participated in the discoveries of the [[Milagro (experiment)|Milagro Experiment]].<ref name=Milagro>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gravity.psu.edu/events/tev_workshop/talks/petra_huentemeyer_tevunid_milagro.pdf |title=Milagro TeV Galactic Unidentified Sources |first=Petra |last=Hüntemeyer |publisher=[[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] |access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref>

Part of her research is dedicated to the study of [[gamma-ray burst]]s with satellite observatories.<ref name=Propel/> The most important result of her work in this area is the discovery of a type of [[Electronvolt|MeV]] energy emission that has been confirmed by the [[Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope|Fermi Telescope]].

Her current lines of research are: study of high-energy emissions from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), study of [[Centaurus A]] as a possible accelerator of ultra-energetic cosmic rays, high-energy gamma-ray astrophysics with the HAWC and Milagro observatories, and installation of high-altitude Atmospheric Cherenkov detectors.

Her working group at the Institute of Astronomy comprises postdoctoral students and students of other academic levels, as well as academic technicians participating in the HAWC project.<ref name=UNAM/>

==Scientific contributions==
As initiator and collaborator on the HAWC observatory, Magdalena González was involved in the discovery of a new [[pulsar]] next to the [[Crab Nebula]]. This discovery provided information valuable in solving the problem of the excess of cosmic [[positron]]s that reach the Earth ([[cosmic ray]]s).<ref name=Milagro/>

She also participated in the first observation of the fusion of a pair of [[neutron star]]s, which was detected by [[gravitational wave]]s and in several [[Electromagnetic radiation|electromagnetic]] wavelengths.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cienciamx.com/index.php/ciencia/universo/18702-descubrimiento-fusion-estrellas-neutrones-ondas-gravitacionales |title=Anuncian descubrimiento de fusión de estrellas de neutrones a partir de ondas gravitacionales |trans-title=Discovery of Fusion of Neutron Stars from Gravitational Waves Announced |first=Tania |last=Robles |work=México Ciencia y Tecnología |location=Mexico City |language=Spanish |date=2017-10-17 |access-date=2019-06-05}}</ref>
